## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khadiravaniyarevatattheragāthā* is a poetic composition belonging to the *Theragāthā* (Thag 14.1) in the Khuddaka Nikāya, preserving verses attributed to the elder Khadiravaniya Revata [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text into nine languages include an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels to individual verses in several canonical Pali discourses, including the *Gandhatthenasutta* (SN 9.14), the *Siṅghapupphajātaka* (Ja 392), and the *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 3.4), as well as internal parallels within the *Theragāthā* in the verses of Sāriputta (Thag 17.2) and Saṅkicca (Thag 11.1) [SuttaCentral]. Beyond Pali, passage parallels are found in Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 32, UVS 32, Uv Kg 32) and Chinese translations of related verse collections (T 212.33, T 213.32) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes resembling parallels in Dhammapada traditions (Dhp 315, G-Dhp 97–134, P-Dhp 216–238, T 210.30, UV 5) and other early suttas (AN 8.29, Snp 2.10, Thig 1.5, Thag 2.38) [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates extensive text reuse within the Pali canon, matching SuttaCentral's curated parallels with *Sāriputtattheragāthā* (Thag 17.2, segments 6.1–11.1 sharing substantial material with 18.4–24.1) and *Saṅkiccattheragāthā* (Thag 11.1, segments 12.1–13.4 identical to 8.1–9.4) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, segments 11.4–13.4 share a stock verse sequence appearing verbatim or near-verbatim in *Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā* (Thag 20.1), *Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.4), and multiple poems of the *Therī-apadāna* (including those of Uppalavaṇṇā, Paṭācārā, Kuṇḍalakesā, Kisāgotamī, Dhammadinnā, and Sakulā) [DharmaNexus]. The verses are cited and explained at length in the Pali commentarial tradition, particularly within the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments are also registered by DharmaNexus with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and Tibetan translations of the *Pratyutpannabuddhasamādhisūtra* (D0133) and *Mahāyānopadeśasūtra* (D0169) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
